title: Dynamic Method Dispatch
summary: Unravel the internal JVM engine of runtime polymorphism: Dynamic Method Dispatch, invokevirtual bytecode instruction, Virtual Method Tables (v-tables), and late binding.
learningObjectives: Understand the exact mechanism of Dynamic Method Dispatch in the Java Virtual Machine
Analyze how Virtual Method Tables (v-tables) resolve overridden methods at runtime
Trace the bytecode instruction 'invokevirtual' and how it differs from 'invokestatic' and 'invokespecial'
Explain late binding (dynamic binding) versus early binding (static binding)
expectedOutcomes: Deep conceptual mastery of JVM internal dispatch mechanisms for high-performance systems
Confidence acing senior-level Java interview questions on v-tables and method resolution

activities.title: Practical Context: Automated Runtime Resolution in the JVM
activities.content:
When an enterprise application executes, thousands of method invocations occur every second across polymorphic hierarchies.

The Java Virtual Machine must resolve which concrete implementation to run without pausing execution or executing costly condition branches.

Dynamic Method Dispatch is the low-level JVM engine that executes this runtime binding with maximum efficiency.

activities.title: Dynamic Method Dispatch: Definition, V-Tables, and Bytecode Mechanics
Simulating Dynamic Dispatch and V-Table Resolution
activities.description: Trace how the JVM resolves method pointers across an inheritance hierarchy.

steps.description: When ref.methodA() is called, JVM inspects SubVTable's v-table; slot A points to SuperVTable.methodA.
When ref.methodB() is called, slot B in SubVTable's v-table points to SubVTable.methodB.
Execution branches dynamically without any if-else conditional instructions in bytecode.

activities.title: Mastery Verification: Dynamic Method Dispatch (10 Questions)

questions.question: What is Dynamic Method Dispatch in Java?
options: Running multiple methods simultaneously on background threads
The runtime mechanism by which an overridden method call is resolved based on the actual heap object
Loading classes over a network socket
questions.explanation: Dynamic Method Dispatch resolves overridden method calls at runtime according to the instance's type.

questions.question: What internal data structure does the JVM use to enable fast dynamic method dispatch?
questions.explanation: The JVM maintains a virtual method table (v-table) containing method pointers for each class.

questions.question: Which JVM bytecode instruction is emitted for invoking a standard overridden public instance method?
questions.explanation: 'invokevirtual' is the standard bytecode instruction for virtual/dynamic method dispatch.

questions.question: Which bytecode instruction is used to invoke a static method?
questions.explanation: 'invokestatic' binds static methods at compile time without any v-table lookup.

questions.question: Which bytecode instruction is used to invoke constructors, private methods, and super calls?
questions.explanation: 'invokespecial' is used for non-virtual methods: private methods, constructors, and super calls.

questions.question: What happens if a subclass does NOT override a method in its v-table?
options: The slot in the v-table is null
The v-table slot points to the superclass implementation
questions.explanation: The subclass v-table simply retains the pointer to the superclass method implementation.

questions.question: What is the difference between early binding and late binding?
options: Early binding occurs before lunch; late binding occurs in the afternoon
Early binding resolves methods at compile time; late binding resolves methods at runtime by inspecting the heap object
Early binding is used for loops; late binding is used for arrays
Early binding is in C; late binding is in Python
questions.explanation: Early binding (static binding) is resolved during compilation; late binding (dynamic binding) is resolved during execution.

questions.question: How does the JIT compiler optimize dynamic method dispatch when a call site repeatedly calls the same subclass?
options: By converting the class to C code
Through monomorphic inlining, bypassing the v-table lookup entirely
By running the code on a different server
questions.explanation: Monomorphic inlining replaces the v-table lookup with direct inlined machine code.

questions.question: Does dynamic method dispatch apply to private methods?
options: Yes, private methods are dynamically dispatched
No, private methods are bound statically at compile time using invokespecial
questions.explanation: Private methods are not virtual and use invokespecial (static binding).

questions.question: Does dynamic method dispatch apply to instance variables (fields)?
options: Yes, fields use field-tables in heap memory
No, fields are resolved at compile time based strictly on the reference type (no dynamic dispatch for fields)
questions.explanation: Fields are never dynamically dispatched. Variable access is bound statically to the reference type.

interviewQA.question: What is Dynamic Method Dispatch and how does it work under the hood in the JVM?
interviewQA.answer: Dynamic Method Dispatch is the mechanism by which a call to an overridden method is resolved at runtime rather than compile time. When a method is called on a reference ('ref.method()'), the JVM bytecode verifier emits 'invokevirtual'. At runtime, the JVM inspects the object header of the instance in the heap to locate its Virtual Method Table (v-table). It reads the function pointer from the v-table offset and branches directly to the subclass implementation.

interviewQA.question: What is a v-table (Virtual Method Table) and how is it structured in memory?
interviewQA.answer: A v-table is an internal data structure created in Metaspace for every class loaded by the JVM. It contains an ordered array of method pointers. Subclasses inherit the layout of their parent's v-table. If a subclass overrides a method, its entry in the table is overwritten with the address of the subclass's code; if not, it retains the pointer to the parent's code. This allows method dispatch in O(1) time.

interviewQA.question: Explain the difference between invokevirtual, invokestatic, and invokespecial.
interviewQA.answer: 1. invokevirtual: Used for normal instance methods; performs dynamic method lookup via v-tables. 2. invokestatic: Used for static methods; bound at compile time to a specific class. 3. invokespecial: Used for non-virtual instance methods: constructors (<init>), private methods, and superclass method calls (super.method()), bypassing v-table lookup.

interviewQA.question: What is Monomorphic Call Site Inlining in HotSpot JIT?
interviewQA.answer: Monomorphic inlining is an advanced JIT compiler optimization. If profiling indicates that an 'invokevirtual' call site always encounters the same concrete class at runtime (monomorphic), the JIT compiler removes the v-table lookup and inlines the target method body directly into the caller, achieving near-zero overhead.

interviewQA.question: Can final methods be optimized differently by the compiler regarding dispatch?
interviewQA.answer: Yes. Because a final method can never be overridden by any subclass, the compiler and JIT know at compile time that no alternative implementation can ever exist. The compiler can generate direct calls or inline the method immediately without worrying about polymorphic invalidation.

interviewQA.question: Why does 'System.out.println(card.type)' access the parent field while 'card.getType()' executes the child method?
interviewQA.answer: In Java, instance variables do not participate in dynamic method dispatch; they are resolved statically at compile time based on the declared reference type. Methods participate in dynamic dispatch via invokevirtual, inspecting the actual heap object. Therefore, card.type reads the parent's field, while card.getType() calls the child's method.

practiceProblems.title: Dynamic Sound Dispatch across Animals
practiceProblems.description: See how the JVM calls the correct animal sound at runtime through an Animal parent reference.
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Demonstrate dynamic method dispatch across animals:

1. Class Animal:
   - Field: protected String name
   - Constructor: Animal(String name)
   - Method: public void makeSound() printing '<name>: Silent'

2. Subclasses extending Animal:
   - Class Lion: constructor(name), @Override makeSound() printing '<name>: Roar!'
   - Class Wolf: constructor(name), @Override makeSound() printing '<name>: Howl!'
   - Class Eagle: constructor(name), @Override makeSound() printing '<name>: Screech!'

Test in Main:
Create Animal[] sanctuary = { new Lion("Lion"), new Wolf("Wolf"), new Eagle("Eagle") };
Loop through sanctuary and call a.makeSound(); on each animal.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Lion: Roar!
Wolf: Howl!
Eagle: Screech!
hints: Iterate with: for (Animal a : animals) a.vocalize();
Witness dynamic dispatch at each step.

practiceProblems.title: Health Check Dispatch across Microservices
practiceProblems.description: Let each service report its own health status through a shared Service parent reference from scratch.
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Build a service health check system using dynamic dispatch from scratch:

1. Class Service:
   - Method 1: public void start() printing 'Base service started'
   - Method 2: public void checkHealth() printing 'Base health: 100% OK'

2. Class Microservice (extends Service):
   - Method: @Override public void checkHealth() printing 'Microservice health: 100% OK (Latency: 12ms)'

Test in Main:
Service s = new Microservice();
Call s.start(); and s.checkHealth();.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Base service started
Microservice health: 100% OK (Latency: 2ms)
Base service stopped
hints: start() and stop() use parent v-table pointers; healthCheck() uses child pointer.

practiceProblems.title: Financial Instrument Yield Calculation
practiceProblems.description: Calculate investment returns for bonds and stocks using a single Instrument reference from scratch.
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Calculate investment yields dynamically from scratch:

1. Class Instrument:
   - Method: public double calculateYield(double investment) returning 0.0

2. Subclasses extending Instrument:
   - Class Bond: @Override calculateYield(double inv) returning inv * 0.045 (4.5% yield)
   - Class Stock: @Override calculateYield(double inv) returning inv * 0.14 (14% yield)

Test in Main:
Instrument inst;
inst = new Bond(); print 'Bond Yield: $' + inst.calculateYield(10000.0);
inst = new Stock(); print 'Stock Yield: $' + inst.calculateYield(10000.0);.
hints: Subclasses override with respective yield calculations.

practiceProblems.title: Fix Static Binding Mistake in Dynamic Dispatch
practiceProblems.description: Static methods do not dispatch dynamically at runtime. Remove static so the child method executes.
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Fix the method declaration so dynamic dispatch works:

Bug: `renderLayout()` was declared `static`. Because static methods bind at compile time, `View v = new MobileView(); v.renderLayout();` prints the desktop layout instead of the mobile layout!

Your Task:
1. Remove `static` from `renderLayout()` in both View and MobileView.
2. Add `@Override` above `renderLayout()` in MobileView.
3. MobileView should print 'Rendering responsive touch mobile layout'.

Test in Main:
View v = new MobileView(); call v.renderLayout();.
hints: Remove 'static' from both Screen and MobileScreen renderUI() methods.

practiceProblems.title: Graphic Rendering Pipeline
practiceProblems.description: Render SVG and Canvas graphics dynamically using a GraphicElement array from scratch.
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Build a graphic rendering pipeline from scratch:

1. Class GraphicElement:
   - Method: public void render() printing 'Rendering generic element'

2. Subclasses extending GraphicElement:
   - Class SvgElement: @Override render() printing 'Rendering SVG: <polygon points="10,10 50,50" />'
   - Class CanvasElement: @Override render() printing 'Rendering Canvas: ctx.drawImage(img, 0, 0)'

Test in Main:
GraphicElement[] elements = { new SvgElement(), new CanvasElement() };
Loop through elements and call e.render(); on each.
hints: RenderPipeline loops over elements invoking render() dynamically.
